title: Enforce jurisdictional KMS blackout and add audit-derivation proxy
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: Introduce a jurisdictional KMS blackout guard and a compact audit-derivation proxy to ensure keys and key-use metadata cannot be used or routed to disallowed regions during compliance windows. Motivation: Recent regulatory reviews and a customer audit highlighted edge cases where operator-initiated key wrapping and emergency operator leases could be directed at out-of-jurisdiction KMS endpoints during degraded routing. The blackout guard provides an explicit, policy-driven hard-fail path that blocks KMS operations when a target region is not allowed for the tenant/service. The audit-derivation proxy constructs a canonical, tamper-evident audit entry that links the residency decision, operator identity, and the KMS key fingerprint and is designed to be compact for high-throughput paths. Design: 1) kms/blackout_guard.go: checks per-tenant jurisdiction policy and the target KMS endpoint before creating or using wrapping tokens. 2) audit/derivation_proxy.go: emits a derived audit record (SHA256 over decision payload + key fingerprint) and attaches the derivation token to existing audit envelopes. 3) internal/rbac/temporal_constraints.go: small RBAC v2 extension that allows ephemeral, timebound operator roles to be annotated with a "geozone-maintenance" constraint; the runtime enforcer rejects elevation if blackout is active. 4) Config: production overlay adds jurisdiction matrix and default blackout windows; feature flags allow staged rollout. Migration and rollout: feature-flagged behind kms_jurisdiction_blackout, default off. We ship as opt-in for tenants with strict residency requirements and enable for internal compliance tests. Rollout plan: opt-in Canary (internal tenants) -> gradual tenant opt-in -> default-on for tenants with residency strictness tag after 60 days. Testing: unit tests for decision logic, integration harness against mock KMS endpoints, end-to-end test that verifies audit derivation appears in the audit store and can be validated. Backwards compatibility: audit derivation is additive and attached to audit envelopes; if downstream consumers ignore it, existing behavior remains. Checklist: - [x] Add blackout guard and decision engine - [x] Add audit derivation proxy and public validation helper - [x] RBAC timebound annotation + enforcer - [x] Config + feature flag wiring - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Documentation updates (console + API) - [x] Release notes and rollout plan Comments: See review thread for a small followup to tighten error codes to canonical gRPC statuses.

review_comments: Markus Nguyen: Please make the blackout decision deterministic when fallback metadata is missing. Right now we fall back to 'allow' which caused a false-negative in the staging run.
Aisha Kapoor: Changed fallback to explicit deny and added unit test that simulates missing metadata. See commit 'init: add blackout guard decision engine and interfaces'.
Evelyn Cho: Audit derivation format looks good but add a public SDK helper to verify derivation tokens and a short example in docs.
Aisha Kapoor: Added VerifyDerivation helper and docs snippet; moved the canonical payload format into audit/payload.go to keep unit test parity.
Diego Morales: Can we ensure the RBAC timebound annotation has deterministic TTL alignment across timezones? We should store TTLs as absolute UTC timestamps in audit records.
Aisha Kapoor: Updated enforcer to canonicalize timestamps to UTC and added tests covering DST transition edge case.
release_notes: Add KMS jurisdiction blackout guard to prevent key usage in disallowed regions and attach a compact audit derivation token to audit envelopes for tamper-evident residency decisions. Feature-flagged rollout; opt-in for tenants with residency requirements. SDK helper added for derivation verification.
notes_for_ops: Operational signals: kms.blackout.denied_count metric and audit.derivation.missing_warning. Alert if denied_count spikes for >1m; derivation missing warnings indicate downstream audit ingestion lag. Telemetry tags: tenant_id,residency_profile,operator_id,decision_reason.
documentation_changes: docs/security/kms-jurisdiction-blackout.md explains configuration, expected audit envelope glue, SDK verification snippet, and rollback procedure.
security_impact: reduces risk by hard-failing KMS calls to disallowed regions and producing cryptographically-derived audit tokens; no secrets introduced. No customer-facing API changes except optional audit enrichment.
